title: Concise hosted endpoint micro-bundle PRD with acceptance gates and launch slate
creator: Leah Chen
summary: Define and deliver a compact bundle of hosted endpoints (concise generation, chat, embeddings, rerank) optimized for PLG onboarding that balances predictable quality, lower cost, and fast time-to-provision. This PRD scopes required surface, acceptance gates, migration constraints, and a stepwise launch slate for Canary -> Regional -> GA.
background: Customers requested a minimal hosted endpoint offering for lightweight integrations and prototypes: a single micro-bundle that exposes concise generation, chat, embeddings, and rerank with pre-configured cost/latency profiles. Existing hosted bundles are feature-rich but have cognitive overhead for new users and higher unit costs for low-volume workloads.
goals: Deliver a single discovery-friendly micro-bundle with sensible defaults for cost and latency
Provide eval-driven acceptance gates to prevent quality regressions
Enable canary and regional rollout with automated fallback to full-hosted lanes
Ship console UX for bundle selection and cost preview
non_goals: Support for private/VPC deployment in initial launch
Re-architecting runtime kernels for new model families
metrics_and_success_criteria: Adoption: 5k unique developers opt-in to micro-bundle in first 60 days
Cost: 20% lower median per-token cost vs standard hosted lane for <5qps workloads
Latency: 95th percentile tail at or below established micro-bundle SLOs (generation <300ms / embeddings <120ms)
Quality: No more than 2% regression on the eval suite compared to baseline model mix
Stability: <1.0% error rate for bundle traffic during regional canary
scope_in: Surface: concise generation endpoint (single-shot generation), chat endpoint (lightweight context), single-vector embeddings endpoint, pairwise rerank endpoint
API: same Redwood API surface with a new 'bundle=concise' parameter and a console selection
Operational: telemetry dashboards (per-bundle cost and latency), canary rollback hooks, automated eval checks
Docs: quickstart guide, pricing table, sample SDK snippets
scope_out: Fine-grained lane-level SLAs beyond bundle defaults
Advanced function-calling or multimodal payloads in launch window
requirements: REQ-1: API accepts bundle=concise flag and maps to pre-configured model/quantization profile
REQ-2: Console selection UI and cost preview for the concise bundle must be implemented
REQ-3: Eval harness must run the canonical test-set nightly and gate merges on regression thresholds
REQ-4: Telemetry events tagged 'bundle=concise' for token counts, latency, errors, and route fallbacks
REQ-5: Canary workflow in infra to route 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback triggers
REQ-6: Fallback policy to compatible standard-hosted lane when concise capacity depleted
REQ-7: Billing changes to support priced micro-bundle SKU and display in invoices
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: API behavior parity for supported operations documented and validated by smoke tests
AC-2: Nightly eval shows no more than 2% quality regression on conversation and rerank evals vs baseline
AC-3: Load test at 2x expected peak for micro-bundle with <1.5x error amplification and stable latencies
AC-4: Console pages show cost preview and clear description; PM+Design sign-off obtained
AC-5: Billing emits SKU 'concise_bundle' and appears in test invoices for sandbox orgs
AC-6: Runbook exists for detecting and rolling back bundle-specific failures; SRE has run a tabletop drill
rollout_plan: Step 0 - Feature freeze and internal dogfood (7 days): enable bundle for Redwood internal orgs and apply nightly eval gating
Step 1 - Canary region (3 days): route 1% traffic in us-west1, monitor eval regressions and error metrics
Step 2 - Expanded canary (5 days): increase to 5-25% with staggered memory/throughput knobs and cost telemetry checks
Step 3 - Multi-region staging (4 days): us-west1 + eu-central1 with cross-region failover validation
Step 4 - Gradual GA (14 days): progressive opt-in for free-tier orgs then open sign-up; monitor adoption and perform two-week post-launch review
launch_checklist: PRs merged: API router changes, bundle mapping table, billing SKU, console UI
Evals: nightly run green for 3 consecutive days and no blocked regressions
Telemetry: dashboards for bundle-level cost, latency, errors provisioned and shared with PM/SRE
Docs: quickstart + migration guide + pricing published and linked in console
Support: Triage runbook and help-center article authored; support rotation scheduled for first 14 days
Compliance: data-retention and audit flags validated for hosted lane; security signoff done if required
Load tests: soak and spike tests executed and artifacts uploaded to GH actions
Rollout playbook: rollback steps and mitigation tested in dry-run
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Eval suite may not cover edge-case prompts leading to undetected regressions -> Mitigation: add focused adversarial prompt set and manual sampling during canary
Risk: Unexpected cost per token for certain request shapes -> Mitigation: create cost-simulation harness and surface per-route cost in console before GA
Risk: Bundle capacity contention with standard lanes under burst -> Mitigation: enforce tenant-aware shaping and automated fallback policy
open_questions: Q1: Should we expose a 'latency_priority' knob for the bundle or keep fixed defaults?
Q2: What is the minimal free-tier credit allocation for developers to try the bundle?
Q3: Do we allow customers to pin a model variant for the bundle in early GA?
